newsitem.title: USA: Woman soldiers say they feared U.S sergeant's rank.
newsitem.headline: Woman soldiers say they feared U.S sergeant's rank.

text.p: The government ended testimony against Army Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson in the Aberdeen Proving Ground sex scandal on Thursday, with three privates saying they feared resisting him because of his rank.

One of the women, a Pennsylvania native, said Simpson warned her if she told anyone, "I'll kill ya." She didn't believe he would actually carry out the threat but did fear military restrictions, she said.

Another private, a four-foot, 11-inch woman from Mississppi who Simpson is charged with raping, said she would run past his office to try to avoid him. She wanted to just get through her schooling and leave the problem behind, she told the military court.
"I hated him with every ounce of energy in my whole body," she said.
Witnesses have described an environment that Simpson, the first to be tried in the Aberdeen scandal, tightly controlled.
Defence counsel Capt. Edward Brady said: "He's prepared to accept responsibility for what he did, but ... only for what he did, not for anything less, and not for anything more."

The defence is due to begin its case Friday. Defence lawyers are expected to call about 20 witnesses to impeach some of the women, to talk about what it means to be a drill sergeant and the options women have to report improper conduct.

Simpson, 32, has been charged with 19 counts of rape and 39 other charges including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment involving 13 women. He has pleaded innocent to those charges but guilty to 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five of propositioning.

The Simpson case is the first trial among 12 soldiers charged in the military's biggest sex scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair, and he has been charged with the most crimes. Four other cases were resolved through plea agreements or administrative proceedings.

The defence said the case had been tainted by overzealous investigators. Under questioning, two of the women said investigators embellished their initial statements. The women however, said they made sure the statements were corrected.
An investigator "would put a lot of words in there to make it juicier, or seem more harsh than it really was," one of the women said.

Much of the testimony of Simpson's alleged victims has been similar. According to witnesses, many of the alleged sexual encounters took place in Simpson's office after he called them there individually.

The 20-year-old private from Tennessee had already been placed on a 90-day disciplinary measure when she said Simpson initiated oral sex and intercourse with her in his office and in her room on two occasions in 1996.

She said Simpson knew staying in the Army was important to her because she had told him so, and he helped her out of the disciplinary matter. When he made the advances, she neither resisted nor reported the incident to authorities, fearing Simpson could have her discharged.
"He was an E-7 and my drill sergeant. I was an E-1, nothing. I had been in trouble before. Even if I did (report the incident), who would believe me?" the private said.
The Clarksburg, Pa., soldier said Simpson first exposed himself to her after being called to his office and allegedly raped her on two other occasions there.
Under cross-examination, the Pennsylvania woman said during the first incident, Simpson asked if he could touch her. But instead of flatly refusing, she told him "No, not here. No, not now."

The final government witness, a 21-year-old from Mississippi, told the court Simpson had intercourse with her five times without her consent. With the exception of one brief attempt, the private never tried to stop Simpson.
The first time they had intercourse, Simpson told her to come to his office. Once there, he began to rub her, told her to remove her clothes and then had sex with her.
"I started crying. He told me then to shut up...I stopped making noise."
